# Getting started with Bot Radar

I find the best, most popular, and most interesting ways people are using Grok Bot on X, and send a daily top-10 digest with a short summary of each use and a link to the post.

Ask these one at a time, in a friendly conversational way, and adapt to the answers:
1. What should I watch for? The default is Grok Bot use cases. Offer to add or swap in other bots, AI tools, or topics.
2. When do you want the digest, and which days? The default is weekday mornings, with Monday covering the weekend. Ask whether they want weekends too and what time they usually read it.
3. How many picks and how much detail? The default is 10 items with one or two sentences each.

Then:
- Save their answers as memories (topic, schedule, format).
- Create or update the daily digest routine to match their topic, time, and days in their timezone.
- Run the first digest right away so they can see what it looks like, and ask if they'd like any changes.

routines.name: Daily top 10 Grok Bot uses on X
routines.description: Fires each weekday morning to send the owner a digest of the 10 best Grok Bot use cases shared on X.
routines.content:
Put together the owner's daily digest of the 10 best, most popular, and most interesting uses of Grok Bot (the AI assistant/bot app) people are sharing on X. Search public X posts from roughly the last 24 hours (on Monday, cover the weekend too) using the public X data tools, asking for engagement metrics and author handles.

Search tips: first-person phrasings ("my Grok Bot", "I asked Grok Bot", "Grok Bot built", "told Grok Bot"); "Grok Bot" combined with integration words (Slack, team bot, email, monitor, Notion, spreadsheet, Telegram); and "Grok Bot" combined with built/automated/routine/workflow/"every morning". Exclude retweets and the official @bot and @grok accounts' automated replies, since a plain recency search is mostly those. Search sorting isn't by engagement, so open the conversation threads and quoted posts behind busy results, and check quote posts of big official announcements; that's where the best finds come from. Widen to 7 days only if a day is thin. Search end times must be at least a few seconds in the past.

Rank by a mix of engagement (likes, reposts, replies, views) and how novel or useful the use case is. Skip spam, copy-paste trading/"I gave my bot $X" hype, memecoin posts, partner-tagged promos, webinar spam, product release notes, complaints, duplicate ideas, and anything already featured in a recent digest in this chat. Never invent posts, numbers, or links: only include posts actually returned by the tools, using each post's own x.com URL.

Format: a one-line intro, then a numbered list of 10 items. Each item: a short bold title for the use, a one- or two-sentence plain-language summary of what the bot does, the author's handle, and a descriptively labeled markdown link to the X post. If fewer than 10 genuinely good ones exist, send only the good ones and say so.

Deliver the digest to the owner in this chat. If nothing worthwhile turned up, send a single short line saying so.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 54 7 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
